name: Husqvarna Battery Repair Kit for BLi200 Batteries
title: Husqvarna BLi200 Battery Repair Kit: Fit and Use
h1: Husqvarna Battery Repair Kit for BLi200 Batteries
meta: Husqvarna BLi200 battery repair kit for 36V battery packs with worn or damaged housing parts. What it fixes, what it doesn't, and when to replace the pack.
tagline: Service parts for Husqvarna BLi200 packs, for crews keeping battery gear in the field.
summary: The Husqvarna BLi200 battery repair kit is a set of service parts for the 36V BLi200 pack, meant for fixing worn or broken outer parts rather than the cells. It is a cheap way to keep a pack in rotation when the housing or latch takes a beating on the truck.
highlights: Made for Husqvarna BLi200 36V battery packs
Covers external service parts, not cells
Keeps a damaged pack in the rotation
Useful for crews running battery top-handle saws and blowers

p: Battery packs on a tree crew live a hard life. They ride loose in the truck box, get dropped from the bucket, and get jammed into a saw with sawdust packed into the slot. The plastic parts usually give up long before the cells do, and a cracked housing or sticky latch is enough to pull a good pack out of service.

This kit gives you the Husqvarna service parts to put a BLi200 back together. Check the parts list against your damage before you order, because it is meant for the outer pack, not for replacing cells or electronics. See the rest of our battery-powered equipment if the pack is past saving.
It also pays to keep a spare pack charged and a small set of service parts in the truck. A battery that goes down mid-climb on a top-handle saw costs more in lost time than the kit costs.

body.h: When to repair and when to replace
p: Repair makes sense when the pack still charges normally, holds a full working day, and shows no swelling, heat, or burnt smell. If any of those warning signs show up, stop using the pack and replace it. Never open the cell compartment or try to bypass the battery electronics.
Keep packs clean and dry, store them at a partial charge over the off-season, and charge them only on a Husqvarna charger. A little care stretches the life of an expensive battery.

faq.q: Does this kit replace the battery cells?
faq.a: No. It is a service kit for the pack's outer parts. A pack with weak, swollen, or overheating cells should be replaced, not repaired.

faq.q: Will it fit other Husqvarna batteries?
faq.a: It is listed for the BLi200. Check the part number against your pack model before ordering for any other battery.

name: Husqvarna Z460 Zero-Turn Mower
title: Husqvarna Z460 Zero-Turn Mower: Overview and Buying Tips
meta: The Husqvarna Z460 zero-turn mower for tree service yards, landscape crews and big properties. What it is good at, what to check on a used one, and upkeep.
tagline: A 60-class residential zero-turn for crews and owners mowing large properties.
summary: The Husqvarna Z460 is a zero-turn riding mower built for large lawns and the mowing side of a tree and landscape business. It turns in its own footprint, which makes trimming around trees, beds, and fence lines faster than a lawn tractor.
highlights: Zero-turn steering for tight trimming around trees
Sized for large residential and light commercial mowing
Good fit for crews that add mowing to tree work
Widely supported Husqvarna dealer and parts network

p: A lot of tree services end up mowing, whether it is their own yard, a few maintenance contracts, or cleanup after a removal. The Z460 is a zero-turn sized for that kind of work: big lawns, open lots, and properties with lots of trees to cut around. Zero-turn steering lets you pivot around a trunk in one pass instead of backing and filling.

Engine, deck size, and options have changed across model years, so confirm the exact configuration on the unit you are looking at. If you are shopping used, the serial plate tells you the year and the parts list that applies. Browse more power equipment for the rest of the cleanup kit.

body.h: Buying used and keeping it running
p: On a used Z460, check the deck for rust-through and bent spindles, look for leaks at the hydrostatic drives, and make sure it tracks straight with both bars forward. Uneven tire pressure and worn belts are cheap fixes; tired drive units are not.

Grease the spindles, change oil and filters on schedule, and sharpen or replace blades often. Never mow slopes steeper than the manual allows, keep the rollover protection in place if fitted, and keep people clear of the discharge.

For tree crews, the mower is mostly about finishing the job. A clean, striped lawn after a removal is what the customer sees last, and that impression is worth having the right machine on the trailer.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna Z460 a commercial mower?
faq.a: It is aimed at large residential and light commercial use. Crews mowing all day, every day, usually step up to a commercial-grade zero-turn.

faq.q: How do I find parts for an older Z460?
faq.a: Use the model and serial number on the frame plate. Husqvarna parts lookups and dealers match parts by those numbers.

name: Husqvarna 525 Series Trimmer Tune-Up Kit
title: Husqvarna 525 Series Trimmer Tune-Up Kit
meta: Husqvarna 525 tune-up kit for 525-series trimmers and brushcutters. The wear parts to replace each season so your trimmer starts easy and runs clean.
tagline: Seasonal service parts for Husqvarna 525-series trimmers and brushcutters.
summary: A Husqvarna 525 tune-up kit bundles the routine wear parts for 525-series trimmers and brushcutters so you can service the machine in one sitting. It is the quickest fix for hard starting, bogging, and poor idle on a trimmer that has gone a season without attention.
highlights: Made for Husqvarna 525-series trimmers and brushcutters
Bundles the routine wear parts in one order
Fixes most hard-start and bogging complaints

body.h: Why a tune-up fixes most trimmer problems
p: A 525-series trimmer that won't start or dies under load usually has nothing wrong with it beyond dirty filters and a tired plug. Dust from brush clearing loads the air filter, old fuel varnishes the fuel filter, and a worn plug makes cold starts a chore. Swapping those parts brings most machines back.
Check the kit contents against your model and serial number before you start, since the 525 family covers several trimmers and brushcutters. Find more service items in our power equipment parts.
A tune-up kit also saves the hunt for individual part numbers. Ordering everything in one go means the trimmer is down for one evening instead of waiting on separate shipments.

Work on a cool engine with the plug wire off. Clean around the filter cover before opening it so debris doesn't fall into the intake. Fish the fuel filter out of the tank with a bent wire, replace it, and set the new plug gap to the spec in your manual.

Use fresh fuel mixed at the ratio Husqvarna specifies, or a premixed fuel if the trimmer sits between jobs. Once it starts, let it warm up and check idle and full throttle. If it still runs poorly after a tune-up, the carburetor may need cleaning.
Write the date on the air filter cover with a paint pen so the whole crew knows when the machine was last serviced.

faq.q: Which trimmers does the 525 tune-up kit fit?
faq.a: It is made for Husqvarna 525-series trimmers and brushcutters. Confirm with your model number, since parts can differ by version.

faq.q: How often should I tune up a trimmer?
faq.a: At least once a season, and more often if you run it daily in dusty brush.

name: Sena Communication Spare Parts Kit
title: Sena Communication Spare Parts Kit for Headsets
meta: Sena spare parts kit for crew communication headsets. Replacement wear parts that keep your tree crew's Bluetooth headsets working and comfortable on the job.
tagline: Wear parts for Sena crew headsets, so a torn cushion doesn't bench a radio.
summary: The Sena spare parts kit holds replacement wear parts for Sena communication headsets used by tree crews. It keeps a headset comfortable and working when cushions, foam, or small fittings wear out after a season of sweat and sawdust.
highlights: Replacement wear parts for Sena headsets
Keeps the crew talking instead of shouting
Good to keep in the truck

body.h: Why spare parts matter on a crew headset
p: Crew headsets take a beating. Ear cushions crack, mic foam tears, and small clips get lost in the chips. A worn cushion lets in noise and loosens the seal, which hurts both hearing protection and how well you hear your groundie over the chipper.

Keeping a spare parts kit in the truck means a small failure gets fixed at lunch instead of benching the headset for the week. Check that the kit matches your Sena model before ordering. More options are in our crew communication section.

Headsets on a tree crew usually go to whoever climbs, runs the chipper, or runs the saw that day, so they get swapped between heads and sweat a lot. Fresh cushions are also more hygienic when a headset is shared across the crew.

Wipe cushions down after a hot day, let headsets dry out overnight, and store them out of direct sun in the cab. Replace cushions as soon as they crack or flatten; a hearing protector that doesn't seal doesn't protect.
Clear communication is a safety tool on a tree job. Agree on standard calls with your crew, confirm every command, and stop work if the radio link drops.
If parts of the electronics stop working, such as the mic or speaker, that is a warranty or service question for Sena rather than something a spare parts kit will fix.

faq.q: Which Sena headsets does this kit fit?
faq.a: It is made for Sena's crew communication headsets. Check your model against the kit's listing before ordering.

faq.q: How often should ear cushions be replaced?
faq.a: When they crack, harden, or stop sealing against your head. On a daily-use headset that is often once or twice a year.

name: 1 in Whoopie Sling
title: 1 in Whoopie Sling: Adjustable Rigging Sling
meta: A 1 in whoopie sling for tree rigging: an adjustable sling you size to the stem for a quick rigging point. How it adjusts, sizing tips, and inspection.
tagline: An adjustable rigging sling sized for big wood and heavy rigging points.
summary: A whoopie sling is an adjustable rigging sling that you can size to the stem in seconds, and this 1 in version is built for heavier wood. It sets a rigging point or holds a block where a fixed-length sling would be too long or too short.
highlights: Adjustable length, sized on the stem
Heavy 1 in rope body for big wood
Pairs with a rigging block or lowering device
Replaces a stack of fixed slings

p: A whoopie sling is a length of hollow-braid rope with a fixed eye at one end and an adjustable eye made by burying the rope inside itself. Pull the tail and the adjustable eye shrinks; pull the eye and it grows. Once it takes load, the bury grips and holds its length.

That adjustability is the point. One whoopie can wrap a small spar or a big stem, so you can set a block at the height you want without tying knots or carrying several fixed slings. Compare other adjustable slings if you need a lighter size.

Match the sling's rated strength to the block, the rigging line, and the loads you plan to catch. The 1 in size is for heavy rigging, not light pruning. Keep the adjustable section tensioned before loading so it doesn't slip as it seats.

Rig only within the rated strength of every component in the system, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Retire a sling that shows cut strands, heavy fuzzing, glazing, or a deformed bury.
Store whoopie slings out of the sun and away from fuel and bar oil, and loosen the adjustable eye between jobs so the bury does not take a permanent set.

faq.q: Can a whoopie sling slip under load?
faq.a: Once tensioned and loaded, the bury grips the rope. Tension it before you load it and make sure the tail exits as the manufacturer intends.

faq.q: Is a 1 in whoopie sling overkill for pruning?
faq.a: Usually. It is meant for heavy rigging. A lighter adjustable sling is easier to handle for small wood.

name: DMM Pinto Pulley with 8mm Ocean Polyester Prusik
title: DMM Pinto Pulley with 8mm Ocean Polyester Prusik
h1: DMM Pinto Pulley and 8mm Ocean Polyester Prusik
meta: DMM Pinto pulley paired with an 8mm Ocean Polyester prusik loop. A compact pulley and hitch combo for tending a friction hitch and building rope systems.
tagline: A compact DMM pulley and 8mm prusik loop for hitch tending and small rope systems.
summary: This combo pairs a DMM Pinto pulley with an 8mm Ocean Polyester prusik loop, giving you a ready-made pulley and hitch set. Climbers use it to tend a friction hitch, and ground crews use it to build quick mechanical advantage and haul systems.
highlights: DMM Pinto pulley with an 8mm prusik loop
Pulley and hitch matched in one purchase
Tends a hitch for smooth slack pulling
Handy for small haul and mechanical advantage setups
Compact enough to ride on the saddle

body.h: How climbers and groundies use it
p: On a moving rope climbing system, a pulley clipped below the friction hitch lets you tend slack with one hand as you advance. The Pinto's side plates let you clip it onto a line without threading the rope end, which is handy when you are already tied in.

On the ground, a pulley with a prusik is the building block of a simple 3:1 for tensioning a rigging line or pulling a tree over. Keep a set in the bag and you can rig one in minutes. See more hitch cord and prusiks for other sizes.
Buying the pulley and prusik together saves matching parts piece by piece, and the combination is a common starting point for climbers moving from a basic hitch setup to a tended system.
An 8 mm prusik needs a host rope larger than itself to grip properly. Test the grip on your own rope before trusting it, since cover, diameter, and wear all change how a hitch holds.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a prusik that is glazed, stiff, or fuzzy, and check the pulley's sheave and side plates for grooves or cracks.
Keep the prusik dry and out of chainsaw oil, which affects grip.

faq.q: What rope will an 8mm prusik grip on?
faq.a: It is intended for host ropes larger than the cord, typically 11 to 13 mm arborist lines. Always test the hitch on your rope before use.

faq.q: Can I use the Pinto for rigging?
faq.a: It is a light pulley meant for climbing and small rope systems. Use rigging blocks rated for the loads of rigging work.

name: Teufelberger tREX 7/8 in Rigging Sling, 20 ft
title: Teufelberger tREX 7/8 in Rigging Sling, 20 ft
h1: Teufelberger tREX 7/8 in Rigging Sling, 20 ft
meta: Teufelberger tREX rigging sling in 7/8 in, about 20 ft long, for heavy removals and big rigging points. Sizing, how crews use it, and inspection tips.
tagline: A heavy 7/8 in tREX sling for big rigging points on serious removals.
summary: The Teufelberger tREX rigging sling is a heavy 7/8 in sling made from Teufelberger's tREX rigging rope, here in a 20 ft length. It is built for wrapping large stems to hang a block or lowering device on big removals.
highlights: Made from Teufelberger tREX rigging rope
Pairs with large blocks and lowering devices

body.h: Where a heavy sling earns its keep
p: When you are blocking down big leaders or catching wood on a removal, the sling holding the block is the anchor for the whole system. A 7/8 in tREX sling gives you the diameter and strength to hang a large block on a big stem, with enough length to wrap a trunk several times or choke it.
Length matters: 20 ft wraps big wood, but on a smaller spar you will have extra to manage. Many crews keep a few lengths on the truck. See other heavy-duty slings to round out your set.
Most crews use a sling like this with a large rigging block, a lowering device at the base, and a rigging line sized to match. All of those parts need to be rated for the same job.

Plan for dynamic loading. A piece that free-falls before the rope comes tight puts far more force on the sling than its weight suggests, so rate the whole system for the shock load and limit the drop.

Rig only within the rated strength of every component in the system, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Retire a sling with cut strands, heavy abrasion, glazing, or a damaged eye.
Store slings clean and dry, out of the sun, and away from saw fuel and bar oil.

faq.q: What block should I use with a 7/8 in sling?
faq.a: A large rigging block rated for the loads you plan to catch, with a sling attachment sized for 7/8 in rope.

faq.q: Is 20 ft too long for most trees?
faq.a: It suits large stems. For smaller wood, a shorter or adjustable sling is easier to manage.

name: Climbing Technology Pillar TG Carabiner
title: CT Pillar TG Auto-Locking Carabiner
meta: The CT Pillar TG carabiner from Climbing Technology: an auto-locking connector for arborist climbing systems. What it suits and how to inspect it.
tagline: An auto-locking Climbing Technology carabiner for tree climbing systems.
summary: The CT Pillar TG carabiner is an auto-locking connector from Climbing Technology for arborist climbing and positioning systems. The auto-locking gate closes and locks on its own, which is what tree work requires on life-support connections.
highlights: Clips bridges, lanyards, and hitch systems
Easy to operate with gloves on

body.h: Where it fits in your kit
p: An arborist carries a handful of carabiners on the saddle: one on the hitch, one or two on the lanyard, and spares for the friction saver or a redirect. Every one on a life-support connection needs an auto-locking gate, so it can't be rolled open by the rope or a branch.
The Pillar TG is CT's auto-locking version of their Pillar carabiner. Check the gate action and size against the rest of your system before you commit, and compare with other auto-locking carabiners.

Climbing Technology is an Italian maker of climbing and work-at-height hardware, and the Pillar line is one of their general-purpose carabiner families. Before you clip it into a life-support system, confirm the markings on the spine show the rating your system requires.
Load a carabiner along its spine, not across the gate or in a three-way pull. Watch for cross-loading on bridges and rings, where a carabiner can roll if it's the wrong shape for the job.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a carabiner that has been dropped onto a hard surface from height, has sharp grooves, or has a gate that doesn't close and lock fully.
Keep carabiners clean and free of grit, and rinse and dry them if they get muddy so the gate keeps closing crisply.

faq.q: Is the Pillar TG suitable for tree climbing?
faq.a: Check that it carries the rating your climbing system requires and that it is auto-locking, as needed for life-support connections under ANSI Z133.

faq.q: What does TG mean?
faq.a: It is part of Climbing Technology's model naming for gate type. Check the manufacturer's information for the exact locking mechanism.

name: Marvin Bull Pruner with Adapter, Double Pulley and Rope
title: Marvin Bull Pruner with Double Pulley and Rope
h1: Marvin Bull Pruner with Adapter, Double Pulley and Rope
meta: The Marvin bull pruner with pole adapter, double pulley and rope: a heavy pole pruner head for thicker limbs. How it cuts, setup on a pole, and blade care.
tagline: A heavy-duty pole pruner head with double-pulley leverage for thicker cuts.
summary: The Marvin bull pruner is a heavy pole pruner head for cutting thicker limbs from the ground or a bucket. This version comes with a pole adapter, a double pulley for extra pulling power, and the rope, ready to mount on a pole.
highlights: Double pulley for more cutting force
Cuts from the ground or bucket
Made by Marvin, a long-time pole tool maker

p: Light pole pruners stall on bigger wood. A bull pruner head has heavier jaws and blade, and the double pulley multiplies the force from your pull on the rope, so you can make clean cuts on limbs that would otherwise need a pole saw.

It works well for clearance pruning, deadwooding, and line-of-sight work where a clean pruning cut matters. Mount it on a pole that matches the adapter and has the reach you need. See more pruners and loppers.
A bull pruner is also handy for deadwood that is too brittle to saw cleanly from a pole, since one decisive cut avoids the bouncing and bark tearing of a long sawing stroke.
Run the rope as shown in the pulley's instructions, and keep it clear of the pole joints so it doesn't bind. Get the hook fully over the limb before pulling, and pull smoothly instead of yanking.

Keep the blade sharp and the pivot clean and lightly oiled. Stay out from under the cut, and never use pole tools near energized lines unless you are a qualified line-clearance worker with a properly rated insulated pole.

Replace a frayed rope right away. A rope that breaks mid-cut leaves the head stuck in the limb, and getting it down can be awkward and risky. Check the pulley wheels turn freely, and clean sap off the blade at the end of the day.

faq.q: Does it come with a pole?
faq.a: No. It includes the head, adapter, double pulley, and rope. Pair it with a pole that fits the adapter.

faq.q: What is the double pulley for?
faq.a: It adds mechanical advantage, so the same pull on the rope gives more cutting force at the blade.

name: Caution Tape, 1000 ft Roll
title: Caution Tape, 1000 ft Roll for Tree Job Sites
meta: Caution tape in a 1000 ft roll for marking drop zones, work areas and hazards on tree jobs. How crews use it to keep people clear and where it falls short.
tagline: Yellow barricade tape for marking drop zones and keeping bystanders out.
summary: Caution tape in a 1000 ft roll is the cheapest way to mark a drop zone and keep bystanders out of a tree job. Crews tie it off between trees, cones, and stakes to set a clear boundary around the work area.
highlights: Marks drop zones and work areas
Ties off to trees, stakes, and cones

p: Every removal and big prune has a drop zone, and the public doesn't know where it is. Tape gives them a visible line. Run it wide enough to cover where wood can land, bounce, or roll, and around the chipper and log loading area.
Tape works with cones and signs, not instead of them. On a road or sidewalk job, follow your traffic control plan and local rules. More options are in our traffic control section.
A 1000 ft roll goes a long way. It covers a big removal with plenty left for the next few jobs, so keep one in each truck instead of rationing a single roll across the crew.
Tape is a warning, not a barrier. Kids, dogs, and curious neighbors will duck under it. Put a ground worker in charge of the perimeter when people are around, and stop cutting when someone walks in.
Pick tape back up at the end of the day. Pieces left in a tree or on a fence make the crew look sloppy and end up as litter.

On residential jobs, tape also tells the homeowner where not to park and where pets need to stay inside. Walk the line with them before work starts so everyone knows the plan. A quick conversation does more than any amount of tape.

faq.q: Is caution tape enough to close a sidewalk?
faq.a: Usually not on its own. Follow local rules and your traffic control plan, which may call for signs, cones, or barricades.

faq.q: How far out should I tape a drop zone?
faq.a: Far enough to cover where wood can land, bounce, or roll. For removals that is often well beyond the tree's height.

name: Jameson Pole End Cap Repair Kit
title: Jameson Pole End Cap Repair Kit
h1: Jameson Pole End Cap Repair Kit
meta: Jameson pole end cap repair kit for fiberglass pruning and pole saw poles. Why the end cap matters, how to replace a worn one, and when to retire the pole.
tagline: A replacement end cap to keep the bottom of a Jameson pole sealed and protected.
summary: The Jameson pole end cap repair kit replaces the worn or missing cap on the bottom of a Jameson pole. A good end cap keeps dirt and moisture out of a fiberglass pole and protects the end from splitting when it's planted on the ground.
highlights: Replaces a worn or lost pole end cap
Keeps dirt and water out of the pole
Protects the pole end from damage
Cheap fix that extends pole life

p: The bottom of a pole gets planted in mud, dragged across driveways, and dropped on its end. Without a cap, the end chips and frays, and dirt and water get inside the tube. That is more than cosmetic on a fiberglass pole, because contamination inside affects how the pole performs.
A new end cap is a cheap fix that keeps a good pole in service. Check that the kit matches your pole diameter and series before ordering. See more poles and kits.
Jameson is a long-time maker of fiberglass poles and pole tools for arborists and utility crews, and replacement parts like this keep its poles serviceable for years.

body.h: Replacing the cap and inspecting the pole
p: Clean the pole end, remove what's left of the old cap, and fit the new one following the kit's instructions. While you have it apart, look over the whole pole for cracks, deep scratches, or fiber showing through the surface.

Wipe poles clean and store them dry and out of the sun. If you work near energized lines, only qualified line-clearance workers should do so, and poles used for that work must be rated, inspected, and tested as the standard requires.
A pole kept clean and capped tends to last longer and is easier to inspect, since dirt and damage are easier to spot on a clean surface.

faq.q: Will this fit any pole?
faq.a: It is made for Jameson poles. Match the cap to your pole's diameter and series.

faq.q: Can I keep using a pole with a cracked end?
faq.a: Fix small end damage with a new cap, but retire a pole with cracks running up the tube.

name: Replacement Lanyard for Hipstar Flex Lanyard
title: Replacement Lanyard for Hipstar Flex Lanyard
h1: Replacement Lanyard for Hipstar Flex Lanyard
meta: Replacement rope for the Hipstar Flex lanyard. Swap a worn rope without replacing the whole positioning lanyard, plus fitting and inspection tips here.
tagline: A replacement rope for the Hipstar Flex adjustable positioning lanyard.
summary: This replacement lanyard is the rope section for the Hipstar Flex lanyard, so you can swap a worn rope and keep the rest of the system. Rope lanyards wear faster than their hardware, and replacing just the rope saves money.
highlights: Replacement rope for the Hipstar Flex lanyard
Reuse your hardware, replace the worn rope
Keeps a familiar setup in service
Saves cost over a complete lanyard

p: A positioning lanyard gets wrapped around bark, saw-scuffed, and loaded at odd angles every day. The rope wears out long before the adjuster and carabiners. Replacing only the rope keeps a setup you already know and saves the cost of a full new lanyard.
Confirm the replacement matches your lanyard model and adjuster before ordering. If you are not sure what you have, compare with other rope lanyards.
Keep the old rope until the new one is installed, so you can compare length, terminations, and the stopper. It's the easiest way to make sure everything matches.
Install the new rope exactly as the manufacturer's instructions show, with the correct terminations and stopper. If you are not sure, have a qualified person check the setup before it goes in a tree.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the adjuster and connectors as closely as the new rope; a fresh rope on worn hardware is still a worn lanyard.
Write the date the new rope went into service in your gear log. It makes retirement decisions easier and is a good habit for any life-support gear.

faq.q: Can I fit this to a different lanyard?
faq.a: It is meant for the Hipstar Flex. Use only parts specified for your lanyard system.

faq.q: When should a lanyard rope be replaced?
faq.a: When it shows cuts, glazing, stiff or soft spots, heavy fuzz, or damage near the terminations.

name: Boom Clip Holder
title: Boom Clip Holder for Bucket Truck Tools
meta: Boom clip holder for bucket trucks and aerial lifts. Keeps pole tools and scabbards secured at the boom so they don't fall or rattle loose while you work.
tagline: A holder that keeps tools secured at the boom of a bucket truck.
summary: A boom clip holder mounts on a bucket truck boom to keep tools secured and within reach. It keeps pole tools and scabbards from sliding around or dropping out while the boom moves.
highlights: Holds tools secure while the boom moves
Keeps tools within reach of the bucket

p: A bucket gets crowded fast: pole saw, pruner, handsaw, rope. Tools that ride loose slide around as the boom swings and can drop on the crew. A clip holder gives a tool a fixed home on the boom, so it's secure while you travel and still in reach when you set up.
Check the mounting style and size against your boom before ordering. More options are in our bucket truck and aerial lift gear.
Bucket crews who prune all day know how much time is lost searching for tools or fishing a dropped one off the ground. A good holder saves that time and keeps the work moving.

Mount the holder where it won't interfere with boom controls, hoses, or the insulated section of the boom. Never mount metal hardware in a way that bridges the insulated portion of an insulated aerial device.
Check the holder and its fasteners at the daily truck inspection. Replace it if it cracks or no longer grips firmly. Keep the area below the bucket clear when you move tools in and out.
A dropped tool from a bucket is a serious hazard to the ground crew. Securing tools at height is part of a good drop-zone plan, along with keeping people out from under the boom.

faq.q: Will a boom clip holder fit any bucket truck?
faq.a: Booms vary. Check the holder's mounting style and size against your truck before ordering.

faq.q: Can I mount it on an insulated boom section?
faq.a: Do not install anything that compromises the insulated section. Follow the truck manufacturer's guidance.

name: Teufelberger 8mm HRC ThermaShield Hitch Cord, by the Foot
title: Teufelberger 8mm HRC ThermaShield Hitch Cord
h1: Teufelberger 8mm HRC ThermaShield Hitch Cord, by the Foot
meta: Teufelberger 8mm HRC ThermaShield hitch cord sold by the foot for tying friction hitches and eye-to-eyes. Fit with your climbing line, cutting, and care.
tagline: Heat-resistant 8 mm hitch cord by the foot, for climbers who tie their own hitches.
summary: Teufelberger 8mm HRC ThermaShield hitch cord is a heat-resistant cord sold by the foot for tying friction hitches. Climbers buy it by length to build their own hitch cords and to suit the hitch they tie.
highlights: Cut the length that suits your hitch

body.h: Why buy hitch cord by the foot
p: Every climber has a hitch they like, and each one uses a different length of cord. Buying by the foot lets you cut a cord to suit a Distel, VT, or Michoacan, and to tie spare lengths. Hitch cord wears fast, so a few extra feet in the truck is cheap insurance.
A friction hitch generates heat on a fast descent, and a heat-resistant cord holds up better. An 8 mm cord is a common size for 11 to 13 mm climbing lines. Browse more tech cordage for other options.
Teufelberger is an Austrian rope maker well known to arborists for climbing lines and cordage, and its hitch cords are made to pair with its own climbing ropes.
Hitch performance depends on the climbing line, the hitch, and wear. Test grip and release low to the ground on your own line before climbing on it.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Hitch cord is a wear item. Retire it when it glazes, stiffens, flattens, or shows cover damage, and never use a cord that has been shock loaded.
Store hitch cord out of the sun and away from fuel and bar oil, and keep track of how long it has been in service.

faq.q: How much hitch cord do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the hitch and how you terminate it. Many climbers buy several feet more than one hitch needs.

faq.q: Can I tie my own eye-to-eye from this cord?
faq.a: Sewn or spliced terminations should be made by a qualified manufacturer. If you tie terminations, use knots approved for the cord and your system, and test them.

name: Jameson CompositLock Poles
title: Jameson CompositLock Poles for Pole Saws and Pruners
meta: Jameson CompositLock poles for building a pole saw or pole pruner setup. How the locking poles fit together, how to pick a length, and pole care tips.
tagline: Locking composite poles for pole saw and pruner heads, for reaching overhead limbs.
summary: Jameson CompositLock poles are locking composite pole sections for mounting pole saw and pruner heads. They let you build the reach you need for pruning from the ground or the bucket and break down for transport.
highlights: Takes pole saw and pruner heads
specs: Pole saw and pole pruner heads

p: Pole work lives on reach and control. Sectional poles let you put together the length you need, then take it apart to fit in the truck. A good locking connection keeps the sections from twisting or pulling apart under the push and pull of sawing.
Check that your saw and pruner heads match the pole's fittings before ordering. See more poles and kits.

Many crews keep a few sections on the truck so they can build a short pole for low clearance work and a long one for higher limbs. Keep sections that go together stored together so they're easy to assemble.
Longer poles flex and get tiring fast, so use only the length you need. Keep the connections clean so they lock fully, and check that each joint has engaged before cutting.

Wipe poles down and store them dry. Retire a pole with cracks or exposed fibers. Stay clear of energized lines unless you are a qualified line-clearance worker using poles rated, inspected, and tested for that work.

Don't use a pole as a pry bar or to knock down hangers. Sideways force can damage the joints and the tube itself. Keep the saw blade guarded when not in use and carry the pole with the head down near the ground.

faq.q: Do CompositLock poles fit other heads?
faq.a: Check the fittings. Heads must match the pole's connection system.

faq.q: Are these poles rated for work near power lines?
faq.a: Only use poles specifically rated and tested for that purpose, and only if you are qualified for line-clearance work.

name: Jameson Hydraulic Pruner Holder
title: Jameson Hydraulic Pruner Holder for Bucket Trucks
meta: Jameson hydraulic pruner holder for bucket trucks. Keeps a hydraulic pruner stored securely at the bucket so it doesn't slide around or fall during work.
tagline: A secure place to store a hydraulic pruner on the bucket.
summary: The Jameson hydraulic pruner holder gives a hydraulic pruner a secure home on a bucket truck. It keeps the tool from sliding around or falling out as the boom moves and keeps it close at hand.
highlights: Holds a hydraulic pruner at the bucket
Keeps the tool secure while the boom moves
Protects the tool and the bucket liner

p: Hydraulic pruners are heavy, and a loose one rattles around the bucket and catches hoses. A holder keeps it in one place, out of your feet and ready to grab. It also keeps the blade from banging into the liner or getting damaged.
Check the holder's fit to your pruner and how it mounts to your bucket before ordering. More options in our bucket truck and aerial lift gear.

Jameson makes a range of pole tools and holders for line clearance and bucket work, so a holder from the same maker is a natural fit for crews already using its gear. Keeping the pruner secured also helps protect expensive hydraulic hoses and couplings.
Mount it where it does not interfere with controls, hoses, or the insulated portion of the boom, and never add hardware that compromises the bucket's insulation or liner.

Disconnect or lock out hydraulic tools as the manufacturer instructs when you put them away. Check the holder and fasteners at the daily inspection and replace a holder that cracks or no longer grips.
A tidy bucket is a safer bucket. Fewer loose tools means less to trip over and less that can fall on the ground crew below.

faq.q: Will it fit my pruner?
faq.a: Check the holder's size against your hydraulic pruner model before ordering.

faq.q: Where should I mount it?
faq.a: Somewhere it won't interfere with controls or hoses and doesn't affect the insulated portion of the bucket or boom.

name: Samson HyperClimb HOT Climbing Line
title: Samson HyperClimb HOT Climbing Line
meta: Samson HyperClimb HOT climbing line, a 24-strand arborist climbing rope in high-visibility colors. Handling, hitch fit, and how to inspect and retire it.
tagline: A 24-strand Samson climbing line in bright colors for tree climbers.
summary: Samson HyperClimb HOT climbing line is a 24-strand arborist climbing rope in high-visibility colors. A 24-strand line has a firm, round cover that runs well through hardware and holds friction hitches predictably.

p: A 24-strand rope uses more, finer strands in the cover than a 16-strand, giving a smoother, rounder rope that tends to hold its shape. Many climbers find it runs through mechanical devices and pulleys easily and grips evenly with a friction hitch.

Bright color helps the ground crew track the line in the canopy and keeps it obvious in a pile of brush. Check diameter and length options before ordering, and compare with other 24-strand climbing ropes.
Samson is a large US rope maker that has supplied arborist climbing and rigging lines for decades, with a wide spread of constructions.
Match your hitch cord and mechanical devices to the rope's diameter, and test hitches low to the ground on a new line. A new rope often feels different until it breaks in.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a rope with cuts, core damage, glazing, flat or lumpy spots, or one that has been shock loaded.
Wash a muddy rope in cool water with a mild soap made for ropes, let it dry out of the sun, and store it in a rope bag. Keep a rope log so you know how old each line is and how hard it has been used.

faq.q: Is HyperClimb HOT good for SRS?
faq.a: Check that your SRS device lists the rope's diameter and type as compatible.

faq.q: What's the difference between 16- and 24-strand?
faq.a: A 24-strand rope has a finer cover that is usually rounder and smoother; 16-strand covers tend to be coarser and more abrasion resistant.

name: Buckingham Alta Verde Climbing Harness
title: Buckingham Alta Verde Climbing Harness
meta: The Buckingham Alta Verde climbing harness for tree work. What to look for in fit and comfort, how to set it up, and how to inspect an arborist saddle.
tagline: A Buckingham arborist climbing harness for working climbers.
summary: The Buckingham Alta Verde climbing harness is an arborist saddle from Buckingham, a long-time maker of climbing and line gear. A saddle is the part of your kit you spend all day in, so fit and comfort matter as much as features.
highlights: Gear loops for tools and hardware

p: A saddle carries your weight, your gear, and your positioning lanyard for hours at a time. Look for a fit that spreads the load across your back and legs, an attachment setup that suits how you climb, and gear loops where your hands expect them.
Check sizing against your waist and leg measurements before ordering. Compare with other Buckingham saddles to see which suits your work.
Buckingham has made climbing saddles, spurs, and lineman gear for a long time, and its saddles are found on plenty of working climbers.

Adjust the waist and leg straps so the saddle sits snug without pinching, then hang in it low to the ground and check comfort before climbing. Set up bridge and attachment points exactly as the manufacturer instructs.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a saddle with cut or worn webbing, damaged stitching, or cracked or corroded buckles, and follow the manufacturer's service life.

Wash and dry the saddle as the manufacturer recommends, keep it away from chainsaw fuel and bar oil, and store it out of the sun. Log its date of first use so you know when it reaches the end of its service life.

faq.q: How do I size the Alta Verde?
faq.a: Use Buckingham's size chart and your waist and leg measurements. A good fit is snug without pinching.

faq.q: Is it suitable for SRS climbing?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions for the attachment points and climbing systems it is approved for.

name: Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt, Green, Large
title: Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt, Green
h1: Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt, Green, Large
meta: Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt in green, size large. A heavy two-layer hoodie for cold mornings on tree jobs. Fit, warmth, and care tips here.
tagline: A heavy two-layer hoodie for cold mornings on the job.
summary: The Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt is a heavy two-layer hoodie made for working outside in cold weather. This listing is the green color in size large.
highlights: From Arborwear, a tree-work clothing brand

p: Tree work starts early, and the first hour is often the coldest. A heavy hoodie keeps you warm loading the truck and setting up, and two layers hold up to brush, bark, and rope better than a thin sweatshirt.
Climbing and running a saw warms you up fast, so plan to shed it once you're moving. Check the size chart before ordering. More cold-weather layers are in our sweatshirts and jackets.

Arborwear makes work clothing aimed at tree climbers and outdoor crews, and the Double Thick line is its heavier take on a classic sweatshirt. Green is a practical color for a job site, because it hides sap and dirt better than lighter colors.
Loose clothing and hood strings can catch in a chipper or saw. Tuck the hood in and remove drawstrings around chippers and stump grinders, and keep clothing snug when working near moving parts.
Wash cold and hang dry to keep the fit. Sawdust and sap come out better with a pre-treat before washing.

Heavy cotton and sweat don't mix well. On hard climbing days, layer a light base underneath so you can take the hoodie off and stay dry. A dry layer to put back on at lunch is a small luxury in winter.

faq.q: How does Arborwear sizing run?
faq.a: Check Arborwear's size chart. A heavy hoodie is often worn a little roomier to layer.

faq.q: Is it OK to wear near a chipper?
faq.a: Keep it snug, tuck the hood, and remove drawstrings. Loose clothing is a hazard near feed rollers.

name: Wire Core Lanyard
title: Wire Core Lanyard for Arborist Climbing
meta: Wire core lanyard for arborists: a cut-resistant positioning flipline for spur climbing and removals. How it works, adjusters, and inspection tips here.
tagline: A cut-resistant flipline with a steel core for spur work and removals.
summary: A wire core lanyard is a positioning flipline with a steel cable core inside a rope cover, built to resist cuts when you work with a chainsaw on spurs. It is the standard choice for many climbers doing removals.
highlights: Steel wire core for cut resistance
Rope cover for grip around the stem
Used with an adjuster on the saddle
Common choice for spur climbing and removals

p: When you're on spurs cutting with a saw, the lanyard is often right in the cut zone. A wire core lanyard has a steel cable inside the rope cover to add cut resistance, which is why many climbers use one for removals.
It is not cut-proof. A running saw can still cut through, so always use a second point of attachment while cutting. Compare all options in our fliplines and lanyards.
Wire core lanyards come in several lengths. A longer one goes around bigger trunks but has more tail to manage. Pick a length that suits the trees you climb most.
Wire core lanyards are stiffer than all-rope versions and work best with an adjuster made for them. Check that the adjuster and connectors are compatible with the lanyard's diameter.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the lanyard if the cover is cut down to the wire, the core is kinked or bird-caged, or the terminations are damaged.
Check the cover for wear where it rubs bark and near the steel core terminations, since that is where damage usually starts. If you can feel the wire through the cover or see broken wires, retire it.

faq.q: Is a wire core lanyard chainsaw-proof?
faq.a: No. It resists cuts but can still be cut. Always use a second attachment when cutting.

faq.q: What adjuster do I need?
faq.a: One rated and designed for the lanyard's diameter and construction. Check the manufacturer's compatibility list.

name: Single Bit Axe Sheath
title: Single Bit Axe Sheath: Blade Cover for Your Axe
meta: A single bit axe sheath to cover the edge when the axe rides in the truck or saw kit. Why a sheath matters, how to get the fit right, and how to keep it up.
tagline: A blade cover that protects your axe edge and your hands in the truck.
summary: A single bit axe sheath covers the edge of a single bit axe so it travels safely in the truck or saw box. It protects the edge from nicks and protects you from the edge when you reach into a tool bin.
highlights: Covers a single bit axe edge
Protects hands reaching into the truck
Cheap protection for an expensive edge

p: A felling axe usually rides in the truck with saws, wedges, and fuel. Without a cover, the edge gets nicked on metal and is a hazard to anyone reaching in. A sheath protects both, and it keeps the edge sharp for driving wedges and limbing.
Check the sheath length and fit against your axe head before ordering, since bit size varies a lot between axes. See more axes and mauls.
Axe sheaths are cheap compared to the time it takes to file out a nicked edge or treat a cut hand. If an axe rides in the truck, it should wear a sheath.
A good fit holds the head without wobbling and keeps the edge fully covered. A loose sheath can slip off, and a tight one can be hard to remove with gloves on.
Keep a leather sheath dry and condition it occasionally so it doesn't crack. Don't store a wet axe in its sheath; let both dry to avoid rust on the head.

Check the sheath now and then for cuts from the edge, loose rivets, or broken straps. A sheath that has been cut through no longer protects anything, and a worn strap lets the sheath slide off on rough roads.

faq.q: Will this fit a double bit axe?
faq.a: No. It is made for single bit axes. A double bit axe needs a sheath that covers both edges.

faq.q: How do I know it fits my axe?
faq.a: Compare the sheath's opening to your axe's bit length and head shape.

name: Jameson 16 in Tri-Cut Wide Saw Blade
title: Jameson 16 in Tri-Cut Wide Saw Blade for Pole Saws
h1: Jameson 16 in Tri-Cut Wide Saw Blade
meta: The Jameson 16 in tri-cut wide saw blade for pole saws. Fast-cutting three-sided teeth for live and dead wood. Fit, cutting tips, and when to replace it.
tagline: A 16 in replacement pole saw blade with fast tri-cut teeth.
summary: The Jameson 16 in tri-cut wide saw blade is a replacement pole saw blade with three-sided teeth that cut on both push and pull. It suits pruning live and dead wood from the ground or a bucket.
highlights: Replacement blade for Jameson pole saw heads

p: Tri-cut teeth are ground on three faces, which helps them cut quickly in both directions. On a pole saw, where every stroke takes effort at the end of a long pole, a fast blade makes a real difference over a day.
A wide blade tracks straighter in the cut. Check the blade mount against your pole saw head before ordering. See more replacement blades.
Sixteen inches is a common pole saw blade length, long enough for medium limbs while staying manageable at full reach. Keep a spare blade in the truck so a broken blade doesn't stop the job.
Undercut heavier limbs first to prevent bark tearing, then finish from above. Let the blade do the work with smooth, full strokes rather than short, hard jabs.

Replace the blade when it starts to bind, wander, or cut slowly. Keep it clean of sap and use a blade guard when transporting. Stay out from under the cut and away from energized lines unless qualified for line-clearance work with rated equipment.
Swap blades with the pole on the ground and the blade guard on, and wear gloves. Check that the mounting hardware is tight before going back to work, since a loose blade wanders and can break.

faq.q: Will it fit my pole saw head?
faq.a: It's designed for Jameson pole saw heads. Check the blade mount and bolt pattern before ordering.

faq.q: Can the blade be sharpened?
faq.a: Tri-cut teeth are usually hardened and most crews replace the blade when it dulls.

name: Sena Crane Operator Headset
title: Sena Crane Operator Headset for Tree Crews
meta: The Sena crane operator headset for crane and tree crews. Clear communication between crane operator and climber on picks. Fit, use, and practical tips.
tagline: A communication headset for crane operators coordinating picks with the crew.
summary: The Sena crane operator headset gives a crane operator clear voice contact with the climber and ground crew during tree removals. It is built for the cab, where the operator needs to hear calls clearly without shouting or hand signals alone.
highlights: Voice contact with climber and crew
Clearer than shouting or hand signals alone

body.h: Why crane picks need clear communication
p: On a crane removal, the climber, the operator, and the ground crew must work in sync. The operator often can't see the cut, so voice calls are critical. A headset gives clear, hands-free contact without relying on shouting over engines.
Check compatibility with the headsets your crew already uses before ordering. More options are in our crew communication section.

Sena makes Bluetooth headsets and intercom systems, and its gear is used by many tree crews to keep the climber, ground crew, and operator talking. Crane work adds pressure: the operator is often far from the tree and can't see the climber's hands.
Agree on standard calls before the first pick, test the link, and have a backup plan with hand signals if the radio drops. Repeat back every command.
Follow the crane manufacturer's procedures and applicable standards, including ANSI Z133 for crane-assisted tree work. Charge headsets daily and keep spares or backup batteries on hand.
Keep a charged spare on the truck for long crane days.

Make sure the headset doesn't block important sounds like alarms or warnings. Keep the volume at a level where you can still hear your surroundings, and take time to fit it comfortably for a long day in the cab.

faq.q: Will it work with my crew's Sena headsets?
faq.a: Check compatibility with your crew's models and the intercom system they use.

faq.q: Do I still need hand signals?
faq.a: Yes. Hand signals are a backup if the radio link drops, and everyone should know them.

name: Yale 10.5mm R.I.N.G. Lanyard
title: Yale 10.5mm R.I.N.G. Lanyard
meta: The Yale 10.5mm R.I.N.G. lanyard for arborist positioning. A rope lanyard from Yale Cordage with a ring termination. Fit, adjusters, and inspection tips.
tagline: A 10.5 mm Yale rope lanyard for positioning in the tree.
summary: The Yale 10.5mm R.I.N.G. lanyard is a rope positioning lanyard from Yale Cordage, built from 10.5 mm rope. It gives climbers a light, flexible lanyard for positioning while working in the canopy.

p: A rope lanyard is lighter and more flexible than a wire core flipline, which makes it the everyday choice for pruning and canopy work. At 10.5 mm, it runs smoothly through many mechanical adjusters.
Check the lanyard length and that your adjuster is approved for 10.5 mm rope before ordering. Compare other rope lanyards.

Yale Cordage is a US maker of arborist climbing and rigging ropes, and it makes lanyards and cordage to go with them. A 10.5 mm rope is a bit lighter in hand than many 11.7 to 13 mm lanyards, which some climbers prefer for long days of pruning.
Rope lanyards are vulnerable to saws. Use a second attachment point when cutting, and keep the lanyard out of the cut path.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a lanyard with cuts, glazing, stiff spots, or damaged terminations.
If you are moving to this lanyard from a thicker one, practice adjusting it low in the tree first, since a thinner rope feeds differently through an adjuster.
Store lanyards clean and dry, away from saw fuel and bar oil and out of the sun. Log the date of first use and inspect before each climb.

faq.q: What does R.I.N.G. refer to?
faq.a: It is Yale's product name for this lanyard. Check the manufacturer's listing for the termination details.

faq.q: Which adjusters work with 10.5 mm rope?
faq.a: Use an adjuster that lists 10.5 mm in its approved rope range.

name: Chipper Knife 10-1/2 x 5 x 5/8 in
title: Chipper Knife 10-1/2 x 5 x 5/8 in
meta: A 10-1/2 x 5 x 5/8 in chipper knife for brush chippers. How to match knives to your machine, when to sharpen or replace, and safe knife changes.
tagline: A replacement brush chipper knife, sized 10-1/2 x 5 x 5/8 in.
summary: This chipper knife measures 10-1/2 x 5 x 5/8 in and replaces worn knives on brush chippers that take that size. Sharp knives feed better, make cleaner chips, and put less strain on the machine.
highlights: Sharp knives feed and chip better

p: Chipper knives vary by length, width, thickness, bolt pattern, and bevel. Match all of these to your chipper's manual or the knives you're replacing, not just the length. A knife that doesn't fit right can damage the drum or disc.
Replace knives as a set so the drum or disc stays balanced. See more chipper knives.
Many crews keep a sharpened spare set on the truck, so a knife change takes minutes instead of a trip to the shop. Rotate sets so one is always ready.

Dull knives slow feeding, make stringy chips, and strain the chipper. Sharpen them before they get badly worn, and keep the bevel at the factory angle. Replace knives that are too narrow after sharpening.

Shut down the chipper, remove the key, wait for everything to stop, and lock the drum or disc before you change knives. Torque bolts to the manufacturer's spec, set the anvil gap, and use new bolts if the manual calls for them.

Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling knives, even dull ones. Clean the knife seats before installing new knives so they sit flat. A knife that doesn't seat flat can work loose. Check bolts after the first few hours of use and inspect knives regularly for chips or cracks.

faq.q: Will this knife fit my chipper?
faq.a: Check the length, width, thickness, bolt pattern, and bevel against your chipper's manual.

faq.q: How often should chipper knives be sharpened?
faq.a: It depends on use and debris. Sharpen when feeding slows or chips get stringy.

name: Marlow Dyneema Throwline 1.8mm x 50m
title: Marlow Dyneema Throwline 1.8mm x 50m
meta: Marlow Dyneema throwline in 1.8mm x 50m for setting climbing lines high in the canopy. Slick, light and strong. Tips on throwing, storage, and care.
tagline: A light, slick Dyneema throwline for setting lines high in the tree.
summary: Marlow Dyneema throwline is a 1.8 mm line on a 50 m spool for setting climbing and rigging lines in the canopy. Dyneema is light and slick, so the line runs smoothly over branches and through crotches.

p: Throwline should be light, slick, and strong enough to pull up your climbing line. Dyneema is very strong for its weight and has a low-friction surface, so the line runs over bark and through tight crotches easily.
At 50 m, there's enough line for tall trees. Pair it with a throw weight that suits your tree and a cube or bag to keep it tangle-free. See more throw line.
Marlow is a British rope maker that supplies arborist, sailing, and industrial ropes, and its throwline is a popular choice for climbers who want something light and fast.
Flake the line into a cube or bag so it feeds without tangling. Check the area before you throw and make sure no one is in the path of the weight.
Throwline is not life-support rope. Use it only to set lines. Replace it when it is frayed or damaged, and keep it clean so it runs smoothly.

A thin, slick line can be hard to grip, especially with gloves. Many climbers prefer to pull the climbing line up with bare hands, then put gloves back on. When pulling up a heavy line, a thin throwline can cut into bare hands, so pull steadily rather than jerking. Store the line in a bag or cube and replace it when the cover frays.

faq.q: Is 1.8 mm throwline strong enough?
faq.a: It is strong enough for pulling climbing and rigging lines into place. It is not for life support.

faq.q: What weight works with it?
faq.a: Most climbers use 10 to 16 oz throw weights, depending on tree height and branch density.

name: Samson Zing-It 2.2mm Throwline
title: Samson Zing-It 2.2mm Throwline
meta: Samson Zing-It 2.2mm throwline: a slick, coated Dyneema line for setting climbing ropes in the canopy. Why the thicker line, how it throws, and care tips.
tagline: A thicker, slick Dyneema throwline that is easier to handle and see.
summary: Samson Zing-It 2.2mm throwline is a slick, coated line made from Dyneema fiber for setting climbing and rigging lines in trees. The 2.2 mm size is thicker than the standard Zing-It, making it easier to handle and grip.
highlights: Easier to grip than thinner throwline

p: Zing-It is one of the most common arborist throwlines because its coating makes it slick and long-lasting. The 2.2 mm size is a bit thicker, so it's easier to grab with gloves, tangles a little less, and is easier to spot in the canopy.
The trade-off is a bit more drag on long throws. Many climbers keep both sizes. Compare with other throw line.
Samson's Zing-It is a staple in many arborist kits, and the line has a reputation for durability. The coating protects the Dyneema fibers from abrasion and helps the line shed dirt and water.
Store the line in a cube or bag so it feeds cleanly, and clear the throw zone before every throw.
Throwline is for setting lines, never for life support. Replace sections that are frayed or flattened, and keep the line clean so the coating lasts longer.

A throwline that is muddy or tangled is slow to use. Rinse it, dry it, and flake it back into the cube at the end of the day. Many climbers cut a damaged section out and retie the throw weight rather than replace the whole line. Use a throw weight matched to the line and the height you need to reach.

faq.q: How does 2.2 mm compare to standard Zing-It?
faq.a: It's thicker and easier to handle, but has a bit more drag on long throws.

faq.q: Can I use Zing-It as a climbing line?
faq.a: No. Throwline is only for setting lines, not for life support.

name: Stein RC2001 Lowering Bollard
title: Stein RC2001 Lowering Bollard for Tree Rigging
meta: The Stein RC2001 lowering bollard: a friction device that mounts to the trunk for controlled lowering of rigged wood. Setup, use, and inspection tips.
tagline: A trunk-mounted lowering device for controlled rigging on removals.
summary: The Stein RC2001 lowering bollard is a friction device that mounts to the base of the tree to control the rigging line while lowering wood. Wrapping the line around the bollard gives the ground crew controlled friction to catch and lower pieces.
highlights: Reduces strain on the ground crew

p: A lowering bollard is a drum fixed to the trunk. The rigging line wraps around it, and the number of wraps sets the friction. The ground crew controls the line, letting it run to lower pieces or locking it off to catch them.
Mounting it to the tree takes the load off the ground worker and puts it into the trunk. Compare with other lowering devices.

Stein is a UK maker of arborist climbing and rigging gear. Bollards like the RC2001 are a common choice for crews who want a dedicated lowering device rather than wrapping the line around the trunk itself.
Mount the bollard firmly following the manufacturer's instructions, and use the number of wraps that suits the load and the line. Keep hands clear of the drum while the line is running.

Rig only within the rated strength of every component in the system, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

Check the bollard, frame, and mounting straps or chains before each job for cracks, wear, or damage. A worn drum can grab or slip unexpectedly. Plan the rigging before the first cut, make sure the ground crew knows the load and the plan, and agree on clear calls between climber and groundie.

faq.q: How many wraps should I use?
faq.a: It depends on the load and the rope. Follow the manufacturer's guidance and adjust for the piece.

faq.q: Can it be used on any tree?
faq.a: It needs a sound trunk that can take the load. Check the manufacturer's instructions for mounting.

name: ISC Ultralink
title: ISC Ultralink Connector for Climbing Systems
meta: The ISC Ultralink, a connector from ISC for arborist climbing and rigging systems. Where it fits, what to check before using it, and inspection tips.
tagline: An ISC connector link for climbing and rigging setups.
summary: The ISC Ultralink is a connector from ISC used to link components in climbing and rigging systems. It provides a secure, compact connection point where a carabiner may be bulky or awkward.
highlights: Alternative to a carabiner in some systems

p: Not every connection in a climbing or rigging system needs a carabiner. A connector link can be lower profile and less prone to cross-loading, which suits semi-permanent connections such as bridges, rope terminations, or device attachments.
Check the Ultralink's ratings, dimensions, and approved uses against your system before ordering. See more climbing hardware.

ISC is a UK maker of rope access and arborist hardware, including pulleys, rigging gear, and connectors. A connector link is the kind of part that often gets overlooked, but it carries the same loads as the rest of the system.
Load a connector link only in the direction the manufacturer specifies, and make sure it is fully closed before loading.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire a connector that is cracked, worn, deformed, or has been shock loaded.
If in doubt about compatibility, ask the manufacturer.

Check that the gate or closure works smoothly and fully locks. Clean and dry hardware after use, especially after exposure to sap, mud, or salt. Retire any connector if you're unsure of its condition. A spare connector costs little compared to the consequences of a failure.

faq.q: Can I use the Ultralink for life support?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer rates it for life support in your configuration. Check ISC's ratings and instructions.

faq.q: Is it a replacement for a carabiner?
faq.a: It can replace a carabiner in some semi-permanent connections. Check the manufacturer's approved uses.

name: Spreader Snap
title: Spreader Snap Hook for Arborist Gear
meta: Spreader snap hook for arborist and tree work. A snap hook for spreading or connecting gear. Uses, choosing a rated snap, and inspection tips here.
tagline: A snap hook for spreading and connecting gear on the job.
summary: A spreader snap is a snap hook used to connect gear and keep straps or lines spread apart. Arborists use snap hooks on lanyards, gear storage, and accessory setups.

body.h: What a spreader snap is for
p: A snap hook clips quickly and holds gear securely. A spreader snap is used where you want to connect gear and keep two straps or lines apart, for example on a gear bag, a tool holder, or an accessory strap.
Check the size, gate opening, and rating against your use before ordering. See more snap hooks.

A good snap feels solid, clips with one hand, and has a gate that snaps shut on its own. Cheap hardware store snaps often have weak springs or sharp edges, which wear straps and slings. A snap with a smooth finish lasts longer and is kinder to the gear it connects.
Only use snap hooks for life support if they are rated and locking as required by the standard. Never use an accessory snap in your climbing system.
Check the gate action, spring, and body for wear, cracks, or corrosion, and replace a snap that doesn't close properly.

Keep accessory snaps clearly separate from your life-support hardware, ideally by color or by where they are stored on the saddle. It avoids grabbing the wrong piece in a hurry. Clean snaps that get gummed up with sap so the gate keeps closing fully, and replace any that rust.

faq.q: Can I use a spreader snap for climbing?
faq.a: Only if it's rated and locking for life support. Accessory snaps should never be used in climbing systems.

faq.q: What should I check before using it?
faq.a: Check the gate, spring, and body for wear, cracks, and corrosion.

name: Yale Double Esterlon 9/16 in Rigging Rope
title: Yale Double Esterlon 9/16 in Rigging Rope
h1: Yale Double Esterlon 9/16 in Rigging Rope
meta: Yale Double Esterlon 9/16 in rigging rope: a double braid polyester line for lowering wood and general rigging. Handling, sizing, splicing, and care tips.
tagline: A 9/16 in double braid polyester rigging line for everyday lowering.
summary: Yale Double Esterlon is a double braid polyester rigging rope, and the 9/16 in size suits everyday lowering and light to medium rigging. Polyester has low stretch and good abrasion resistance, so it handles well on blocks and lowering devices.

p: A 9/16 in rigging line is a common size for pruning and light to medium removals. It's big enough for a lot of everyday wood, but still easy to handle and run through blocks and lowering devices.
Double braid polyester keeps its shape well and splices cleanly for eyes and slings. Compare with other rigging rope.

Yale Cordage makes rigging lines for arborists, and Double Esterlon is one of its long-standing polyester double braids. Many crews like it for the way it runs through blocks and lowering devices without much stretch.
Size your rope to the loads you plan to catch, accounting for dynamic loading. A small piece dropped a long way can exceed the rope's capacity.

Rig only within the rated strength of every component in the system, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Retire rope with cuts, heavy abrasion, glazing, or core damage.

Keep the rope clean and dry, store it in a rope bag out of the sun, and keep it away from fuel and bar oil. Track rope age and use with a log. A rigging line takes repeated shock loads, so inspect it often. Retire rope that feels stiff, has flat spots, or shows heavy glazing from friction.

faq.q: Is 9/16 in strong enough for removals?
faq.a: For light to medium removals, often yes. Heavy wood calls for a larger rope and rated components.

faq.q: Can I splice Double Esterlon?
faq.a: Yes, with the double braid splicing method. Have splices done by a trained splicer.
